clue.text: Presumably fast delivery man's returned bonus?

definitions.text: Presumably fast delivery man's returned bonus?

parts.words: Presumably fast delivery man's returned bonus?
parts.note: a cricket bowler who delivers fast presumably has his spin switched off, and a by-product or bonus result is also described by this hyphenated term

explanation.surface: A courier who drives quickly gets his bonus back.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler's ball is a delivery; a fast bowler does not use spin, so for him spin is 'off'. The whole reads as a cryptic description of a by-product.
explanation.definitionFit: A by-product or incidental benefit arising from something else is a bonus outcome of that kind.

clue.text: Stage exercises for drilling marines

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

indicators.note: drilling means boring into, so the word for goes into the marines' letters

parts.note: RM stands for the Royal Marines
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sergeant puts on physical training to drill a squad of marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drilling' looks like military drill but signals that FOR bores into RM.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage a play is to put it on, a synonym for presenting it to an audience.

clue.text: Beef served up to newspaper girl

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to beef is to complain, to moan
the i is a British newspaper, and I is also short for The Independent

explanation.surface: Some beef is dished up for the girl who delivers papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns MOAN into NAOM in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name from the Bible, here clued by a word for a young woman.

clue.text: Medicine for one is not working around college

indicators.note: around means the broken-down word encloses the college letter

parts.note: a machine that is not working is faulty

explanation.surface: A medicine that fails around a college campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medicine for one' means medicine as an example of a university department.
explanation.definitionFit: A university department or school of study, such as medicine or law, is an example of this.

clue.text: Nasty smell in Barking store starts again …

indicators.note: in puts the smell inside the rearranged shop letters
barking means mad, so the letters of store go crazy

parts.note: BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A bad smell in a shop in Barking, a London district, comes back again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' (mad) is the anagram signal; it is also a district of east London, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart a computer is to switch it off and on again, the sense of starting again.

clue.text: Conquistador promotes last pair to head bodyguard

indicators.note: in a down clue, promotes means moves up, so the final two letters go to the top

parts.note: Hernan Cortes was the Spanish conquistador who conquered Mexico

explanation.surface: A conquistador promotes two men to lead his guard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotes last pair to head' moves ES from the end of CORTES to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who accompanies a person for protection is an escort, an armed guard.

clue.text: Foot's 17, getting on with delivery process

parts.note: someone getting on in years is old
labour is the process of giving birth, delivering a baby

explanation.surface: An ageing foot is coming along in its giving birth.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party in the early 1980s, before its New Labour rebranding.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional left-wing form of the Labour Party, before the 1990s rebrand, was the party Michael Foot led.

clue.text: Beat guy, 23

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat them
a gent is a gentleman, a guy

explanation.surface: Thrash the fellow, as per instruction 23.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across, in its mathematical sense, is a trigonometric function.
explanation.definitionFit: In trigonometry, sine, cosine and this ratio are all mathematical functions.

clue.text: Feature of cryptic game? An ingenue tackles it

definitions.text: Feature of cryptic game? An ingenue tackles it

parts.words: Feature of cryptic game? An ingenue tackles it
parts.note: crossword clues often conceal a word within a run of letters, and here the word meaning sense is concealed across the words game and An ingenue

explanation.surface: A newcomer tries a puzzle known for its tricky clues.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does what it describes: MEANING lies concealed in 'gaME AN INGenue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword clues conceal a secondary sense behind their surface, so a concealed significance is their defining feature.

clue.text: … so I must ring head of Rentokil

indicators.note: must ring means the self word circles round the letter that follows

parts.note: the ego is the self, the I

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the pest-control firm's name

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: so I'd better phone the boss of the pest controllers.
explanation.walkthrough: Rentokil is a British pest-control company; the ellipsis links this clue's surface to the smell in 5 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin word meaning therefore, used to draw a conclusion, just as 'so' can be.

clue.text: Money (not much of it) I'd invested in agreement

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money

indicators.note: invested means placed inside, like money put into a fund, so the I'd letters go into the small coin

parts.note: a cent is a small amount of money
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A small sum of money I put into a deal on which we agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' in the bracket refers back to 'Money', so 'not much of it' is a small coin.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that coincide happen together or correspond, so they are in agreement.

clue.text: Spies infiltrate very large 17

indicators.note: spies who infiltrate get inside, so their letters go into the others

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
L is the clothing size abbreviation for large
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: Agents infiltrate a very large political organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is a party in the sense of a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is an informal gathering or get-together, one kind of party.

clue.text: Old man raves about king in early medieval period

parts.note: da is an informal word for father, an old man

indicators.note: about means the raging word goes round the royal letter

parts.note: to rave is to rage
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A father rants about the monarch of an earlier age.
explanation.definitionFit: The centuries after the fall of Rome in western Europe are traditionally called this, a period of supposed ignorance.

clue.text: Taking on scheme in eastern China

indicators.note: in places the scheme word inside the dynasty word

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China, and Ming is also fine Chinese porcelain
a ploy is a scheme or stratagem

explanation.surface: Hiring under some scheme in the east of China.
explanation.definitionFit: Employing staff means hiring them, which is taking them on.

clue.text: It's clear to me ground delayed arrival

indicators.note: ground as in ground down or crushed, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they plainly arrived late on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun but is the past tense of grind, scrambling CLEAR TO ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns up after the start is a late arrival, a person delayed in coming.

clue.text: Son opens pockets for Poles

indicators.note: opens means the son letter splits the pocketing word apart

parts.note: in snooker a player pockets or pots a ball
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son opens pockets to find people from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like nationality, but means wooden stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright stakes or wooden supports are synonyms for poles.

clue.text: Maybe Labour is not entirely ignoring Left

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the letter for left

parts.note: something partly so is not entirely so

explanation.surface: Perhaps the Labour movement is not wholly disregarding the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a British political party, given here as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Labour movement is an example of a political organisation, so 'maybe' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: A top conductor on trial, none shrewder

parts.note: Cu is the symbol for copper, one of the best conductors of electricity
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A leading orchestra conductor on trial, and no one is sharper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top conductor' suggests a maestro but means copper, an excellent electrical conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word meaning sharp-witted, so the most perceptive, with nobody shrewder.

clue.text: Observe speed of star?

parts.note: a celeb is a celebrity, a star
a rate is a speed

explanation.surface: Watch how fast a star moves across the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' suggests astronomy but means a famous person; 'speed of star' gives the celebrity word followed by the speed word.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe a festival or anniversary is to mark it with festivities.

clue.text: Jaguar tours county in special race

indicators.note: tours means goes around, so the car word encloses the county letters

parts.note: the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A Jaguar driving around a county in a special race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' suggests motor racing but means a biological population.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology, a population of a species adapted to local conditions is a distinct race or variety.

clue.text: During tremors 2 manoeuvres

indicators.note: During means occurring inside, so the stage word sits within the twitches

parts.note: tics are involuntary twitches or tremors
the answer to 2 down means to stage, and to act is to put on a stage show

explanation.surface: Military manoeuvres staged during an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 2 points to 2 down, whose sense 'stage' leads to ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Planned moves to gain an advantage, as in military or sporting strategy, are manoeuvres.

clue.text: Berliner's article describing pub food

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing round, so the article goes round the pub

parts.note: der is the German masculine definite article, as a Berliner would say it
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A German writes a piece about food in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' looks like writing about, but means tracing a line around.
explanation.definitionFit: The main meal of the day is a serving of food.

clue.text: 17 force court to stop marriage

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the court letters go inside the marriage word

parts.note: a marriage is a union

explanation.surface: A party forces the court to halt a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 across is a party in the sense of a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal social event such as a reception or dinner dance counts as a party.

clue.text: One of 16 no longer held in reserve?

definitions.meaning: 16 across means positions or jobs, and a position of responsibility is an example
something kept on ice is held back for later; once taken out it is literally no longer on ice

explanation.surface: A post that has been released from the reserve list.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into two: the reverse of 'on ice', the idiom for being kept in reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A post such as treasurer or chairman is a position of authority, one of the posts of 16.

clue.text: Big 22 perhaps lent banks euros

indicators.note: banks as a verb means surrounds like a river's banks, so the fast word goes around the euro letter

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting, so lent suggests a fast
E is the abbreviation for euros

explanation.surface: A big lender perhaps lent money that the banks held in euros.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lent' looks like the past of lend but is the season of fasting; 22 down is a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquet is a large, lavish meal, so a big dinner is an example of one.

clue.text: Stability for each worker within French city limits

parts.note: per means for each
a man is a worker, as in a staff member
en is French for in or within

indicators.note: limits are the boundaries, so the first and last letters of city

explanation.surface: Stability for each employee inside the borders of a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French city' looks like one phrase, but splits: 'within French' is the French word for in, and 'limits' takes the ends of 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of lasting unchanged is steadiness or stability.

clue.text: Amateur teams form league

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a football or cricket team, so XIS are teams

explanation.surface: Amateur sides come together to make up a sports league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'league' suggests sport but means an alliance, as with the wartime powers.
explanation.definitionFit: The alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan in the Second World War was called this, a league of nations.

clue.text: Dish prison reformer there

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
Elizabeth Fry was a famous English prison reformer

explanation.surface: A prison reformer serves a dish there.
explanation.definitionFit: Quickly fried chopped food cooked in a wok is a popular dish.

clue.text: Student is trying to impress oral examiner

indicators.note: to impress here means to press into or hold within, so the answer is held inside the words

explanation.surface: A student hopes to win over the examiner in a spoken exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral examiner' suggests a viva but means someone who examines mouths.
explanation.definitionFit: A tooth doctor examines the mouth, so is literally an examiner of the oral cavity.
